sub: Named after “the moon” (al-qamar), which splits in ayah 1
theme: A warning to Makkah’s deniers, who saw the moon split and called it magic. Five earlier nations denied their messengers and were destroyed. The Quran is made easy to remember: will anyone take heed?
story: Revealed in Makkah, about five years before the Hijrah. At Minā the Makkans asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign, and the moon split into two halves with a mountain between them. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Be witnesses.”

The Quraysh said, “He has bewitched you,” and decided to ask travellers arriving from elsewhere, since he could not bewitch everyone. The travellers said they had seen it too. Still the deniers turned away and called it passing magic.

The surah answers them with five nations who denied their messengers and were destroyed, each story closed by the same refrains. The Prophet ﷺ used to recite it, with Sūrat Qāf, at the two ʿĪd prayers.

sections.title: The moon splits, deniers cry magic; they’ll rush out to the Caller
sections.meaning: The Hour is near and the moon has split. Yet whenever the deniers see a sign they turn away and call it passing magic, following their desires. Warnings from past nations already reached them, and did nothing. So leave them until the Caller calls, and they pour from their graves like locusts.
points: The Hour is near; the moon has split
They see a sign, call it magic, and follow their desires
Deterring news and perfect wisdom came, but warnings don’t help
Leave them: eyes lowered, they pour from graves like locusts
Racing to the Caller: “This is a hard Day”
sections.matters: It sets out the charge the whole surah answers: they saw a clear sign and still called it magic. The stories that follow are the “news with deterrence in it” of ayah 4, and the Day of ayat 6–8 is where all denial ends.
sections.story: The Makkans asked for a sign and the moon split in two. The Prophet ﷺ said, “Be witnesses.” They said he had bewitched them, asked arriving travellers, heard that they had seen it too, and still denied.
explained: Iqtarabat as-sāʿah: the Hour has drawn near, and the moon split as a sign of it. If the moon can split, the whole universe can break apart. But the deniers turned away and said siḥrun mustamirr: magic that will soon fade, or powerful magic. Every sign got the same answer, because they followed their desires.

Yet kullu amrin mustaqirr: every matter reaches its settled end. The news of destroyed nations had reached them, full of wisdom, and warnings still did nothing. So turn from them. On the Day the Caller calls, they rush from the graves like spreading locusts, eyes lowered, saying: “This is a hard Day.”
teaches: A heart set on its desires will explain away any sign.
Every matter reaches its end; the truth always comes out.
Learn from other nations’ history before you become the lesson.
That Day is hard for the deniers, not for the believers.
sections.hook: As-sāʿah opens the surah (1) and returns twice in 46. Ad-dāʿ, the Caller, appears at 6 and 8. Don’t swap mustamirr (2) and mustaqirr (3): each returns once, at 19 and 38.

sections.title: Noah’s people call him mad; the flood drowns them, the ark sails
sections.meaning: Before Makkah, Noah’s people denied Allah’s servant, called him mad and drove him off. He cried: I am overpowered, so help. The sky poured, the earth burst with springs, and the waters met as decreed. Noah sailed on a ship of planks and nails, under Allah’s eyes. Is there anyone who will take heed?
points: Noah’s people deny Our servant: “A madman!” He is driven off
He calls his Lord: I am overpowered, so help
Sky pours, earth bursts with springs; the waters meet as decreed
Carried on planks and nails, sailing under Our eyes
Left as a sign; how was My punishment? The Quran is made easy
sections.matters: The first of five stories sets the pattern the rest repeat: a messenger is denied, the punishment comes, and refrains close it. Its last ayah gives the surah’s central call: the Quran is made easy to remember, so who will take heed?
sections.story: No specific incident. “Before them” means before the Quraysh: after their denial, they are warned with what happened to earlier nations, starting with Noah’s people.
explained: Noah called his people to worship Allah alone. They called him majnūn, mad, and wazdujir: he was rebuked, threatened with stoning, and driven off. Only a few believed, and they could not resist the rest. So Noah prayed: “I am overpowered, so help.”

Allah opened the gates of the sky with pouring water and made the earth burst with springs. The two waters met for a matter already decreed: the drowning of the deniers. Noah was carried on a ship of planks and nails, sailing under Allah’s eyes, a reward for the one they had rejected. It was left as a sign.
teaches: Rejecting a messenger always ends the same way.
When you are overpowered, turn to Allah: “So help.”
Allah watches over those who carry His message.
The Quran is easy to memorize and to take heed from, so take it.
sections.hook: Story 1 of 5: Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, Lot, Pharaoh. It opens with kadhdhabat (9), like the next three. Three refrains close it back to back: fahal min muddakir (15), fa-kayfa (16), yassarnā (17).

sections.title: ʿĀd deny; a violent wind tears them out like uprooted palm trunks
sections.meaning: ʿĀd, the people of Hūd, denied too. How was My punishment and warning? A freezing, roaring wind struck them on a day of lasting misfortune. It plucked people up and threw them down like palm trunks torn from their roots. How was My punishment? The Quran is made easy: will anyone take heed?
points: ʿĀd deny; how was My punishment and warning?
A furious wind on a day of lasting misfortune
Tearing people out like uprooted palm trunks
How was My punishment? The Quran is made easy
sections.matters: The shortest full story, just five ayat. It shows how little the strongest, tallest people are once they defy Allah. Its question comes twice, before the wind and after it, and its last ayah closes the surah’s first ruku.
sections.story: No specific incident. ʿĀd were the people of Hūd, sent to call them to worship Allah alone. They denied him, as Noah’s people had denied Noah.
explained: ʿĀd denied their messenger, and before the punishment is even described the question comes: how was My punishment and My warning? Allah sent a ṣarṣar wind, bitterly cold and roaring, on a day of naḥs mustamirr: misfortune that kept going, for seven nights and eight days, and led straight into the punishment of the Hereafter.

The wind tore them from the ground, lifted them high and threw them down on their heads. Their bodies lay like aʿjāz nakhl munqaʿir, the trunks of palm trees ripped from their roots; they were a tall people. How was My punishment? The Quran is made easy: will anyone take heed?
teaches: Strength and size protect no one who defies Allah.
Allah’s warning comes before His punishment, so heed it early.
The refrain repeats out of mercy: Allah keeps calling us back.
sections.hook: Story 2: ʿĀd, the shortest. Fa-kayfa kāna ʿadhābī wa nudhur comes twice, inside its first ayah (18) and at 21. Innā arsalnā ʿalayhim (19) returns for Thamūd (31) and Lot (34).

sections.title: Thamūd scorn a lone human messenger, kill the she-camel, then one blast
sections.meaning: Thamūd denied the warnings: follow one man from among us? He is an arrogant liar! Tomorrow they will know who the liar is. Allah sent the she-camel as a test, with the water shared by turns. They called their man, and he killed her. One blast came, and they became like trampled twigs.
points: Follow one human from among us? He’s an arrogant liar
Tomorrow they will know who the arrogant liar is
The she-camel as a test; the water shared by turns
They call their man, he kills her; how was My punishment?
One blast: like dry twigs of a pen. The Quran is easy
sections.matters: Their objection is the one deniers always raise against messengers: why him, a man like us? The she-camel shows that even a sign they asked for did not move them, and a single blast ends a whole nation.
sections.story: No specific incident. Thamūd were the people of Ṣāliḥ. They asked him for a she-camel from a rock, and Allah sent her as a test: one day of water for her, one day for them.
explained: Thamūd scoffed: follow a human, just one of us? Then we would be in ḍalāl wa suʿur, error and madness. Why would the message come to him alone? He is kadhdhābun ashir, an arrogant liar. Allah answers: tomorrow they will know who the arrogant liar really is.

The she-camel came as a test, so Ṣāliḥ was told to watch and be patient. The water was shared, each turn kept. They grew tired of it and called their most wretched man, who took his sword and killed her. How was My punishment? One ṣayḥah, a single blast, and they were like crumbled dry twigs from an animal pen.
teaches: Being an ordinary human never disproves a messenger.
A sign you demanded is a test, not a guarantee.
Watch and be patient: the better end belongs to the messenger.
The people called for the killing, and the whole people were punished.
sections.hook: Story 3: Thamūd, the longest. Kadhdhabat Thamūdu bin-nudhur (23) matches Lot’s opener (33) exactly. Wāḥid twice: “one human” (24), “one blast” (31). Here fa-kayfa (30) comes before the punishment ayah.

sections.title: Lot’s people demand his guests; stones rain, his family saved before dawn
sections.meaning: Lot’s people denied the warnings. A storm of stones struck them, but Lot’s family was saved before dawn, a favour: this is how Allah rewards the grateful. Lot had warned them, and they argued. They demanded his guests, so Allah blinded them. A lasting punishment struck at daybreak. Taste My punishment and warning!
points: Lot’s people deny; stones rain, his family saved before dawn
A favour from Us: so We reward the grateful
He had warned them; they disputed the warnings
They demand his guests; their eyes wiped out: “Taste!”
A lasting punishment at dawn; taste it. The Quran is easy
sections.matters: This story puts rescue beside punishment: the grateful are saved before dawn. Its refrain also changes from a question, how was My punishment, to a command: taste My punishment. Its last ayah gives the full refrain for the final time.
sections.story: No specific incident. Lot called his people to worship Allah alone and forbade an immoral act no people had done before. Angels came to him as guests, and his people came demanding them.
explained: Lot’s people denied the warnings. Allah sent a ḥāṣib, a wind hurling stones, on all but Lot’s family, whom He saved bi-saḥar, in the last part of the night. Lot left with his daughters; his wife met her people’s fate. The rescue was a favour, and this is how Allah rewards whoever is grateful.

Lot had warned them of Allah’s grip, but they argued the warning away. When angels came to him as handsome young guests, his people rushed to his door demanding them. Allah wiped out their eyes, leaving their faces smooth: taste My punishment. At daybreak a lasting punishment struck, and their towns were turned upside down.
teaches: Gratitude to Allah is a cause of rescue.
Arguing a warning away doesn’t cancel it.
Allah defends His messengers when no one else can.
Punishment can strike by morning; never assume there is time.
sections.hook: Story 4: Lot. No fa-kayfa here: the refrain becomes fa-dhūqū ʿadhābī wa nudhur, twice (37, 39). Bi-saḥar (34) rhymes with man shakar (35). Yassarnā appears for the fourth and last time at 40.

sections.title: Pharaoh seized; Makkah’s crowd will flee; all is decreed; the righteous honoured
sections.meaning: Pharaoh’s people denied every sign and were seized. Are Makkah’s deniers any better, or immune? Their united crowd will be routed, and the Hour is worse. Criminals are dragged into the Fire on their faces. Allah created everything by decree, and every deed is written. The righteous sit near the All-Powerful King.
points: Pharaoh’s people deny every sign; seized by the Mighty, All-Powerful
Are your disbelievers better, or immune? Or: “We are a winning crowd”?
The crowd will be routed; the Hour is worse and more bitter
Criminals dragged on their faces: “Taste the touch of Saqar”
Everything created by decree; Our command is one, like a blink
Your kind were destroyed; every deed, small or great, is written
The righteous in gardens and rivers, near the All-Powerful King
sections.matters: Here the stories turn on the listener: if five mighty nations fell, Makkah’s deniers are no exception. It foretells their army’s defeat, which came at Badr, and ends on the surah’s two outcomes: dragged on faces, or seated in honour near Allah.
sections.story: Reportedly Abū Jahl boasted at Badr, “We will win today,” and 44–45 came down; other reports place them in Makkah, understood only at Badr. Ayat 47–49 reportedly answered the Quraysh when they argued with the Prophet ﷺ about decree.
explained: Warnings came to Pharaoh’s people through Moses and Aaron. They denied all nine signs, so Allah seized them as the Mighty, All-Powerful, and drowned them. Then Makkah is asked: are your disbelievers better than those nations, or is your immunity written in scripture? Or do you trust your numbers? The crowd will be routed, and the Hour is worse.

The criminals are lost and will burn, dragged into the Fire on their faces: taste the touch of Saqar. Allah created everything bi-qadar, by measure and decree, and His command is one word, faster than a blink. Every deed, small or great, is written. The righteous sit in gardens and rivers, in a seat of truth near the All-Powerful King.
teaches: No people are exempt from Allah’s law just for being who they are.
Numbers and alliances cannot stop what Allah has decreed.
Everything happens by Allah’s measure and decree.
Small deeds are written too, so never belittle a sin.
The seat of honour near Allah is for the righteous.
sections.hook: Story 5: Pharaoh, two ayat, no refrain, opening wa laqad jāʾa (41), not kadhdhabat. Pairs: muqtadir (42, 55), fī az-zubur (43, 52), ḍalālin wa suʿur (24, 47). Fahal min muddakir returns alone at 51.

groups.text: The Hour is near and the moon has split. The deniers call every sign passing magic and follow their desires.
Warnings from past nations reached them, full of wisdom, but warnings do nothing for those who refuse.
Leave them until the Caller calls: they pour from the graves like locusts, eyes lowered, saying, “This is a hard Day.”
Noah’s people called him mad and drove him off, so he prayed: “I am overpowered, so help.”
Rain poured from the sky, springs burst from the earth, and the waters met as decreed.
Noah sailed on a ship of planks and nails, under Allah’s eyes, a reward for the one rejected.
It was left as a sign. How was My punishment and warning? The Quran is easy: will anyone take heed?
ʿĀd denied. A freezing, roaring wind on a day of lasting misfortune tore them out like uprooted palm trunks.
How was My punishment and warning? The Quran is easy: will anyone take heed?
Thamūd refused to follow one human and called him an arrogant liar. Tomorrow they will know who the liar is.
The she-camel came as a test, with the water shared by turns. They called their man, and he killed her.
How was My punishment? One blast, and they became like dry twigs of a pen. The Quran is easy.
Lot’s people denied. Stones rained on them, but Lot’s family was saved before dawn, a reward for gratitude.
They argued away his warning and demanded his guests, so Allah blinded them: taste My punishment.
A lasting punishment struck at dawn. Taste My punishment and warning. The Quran is easy: will anyone take heed?
Warnings came to Pharaoh’s people. They denied every sign, and the Mighty, All-Powerful seized them.
Are Makkah’s deniers better, or immune? Their crowd will be routed, and the Hour is worse and more bitter.
The criminals are lost and will burn, dragged on their faces: taste the touch of Saqar.
Allah created everything by decree, and His command is a single word, quicker than a blink.
Your kind were destroyed before. Every deed they did, small or great, is written down.
The righteous are in gardens and rivers, in a seat of truth near the All-Powerful King.

1.explain: Iqtarabat as-sāʿah: the Hour has drawn near. Wanshaqqa al-qamar: the moon split in two in the Prophet’s ﷺ time, as a sign; people saw a mountain between the halves. One view held it is still to come.
1.why: The Makkans asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign, and the moon split in two. He ﷺ said, “Be witnesses.” They claimed he had bewitched them, but arriving travellers confirmed they had seen it too, and ayat 1–2 came down.

2.explain: Whenever they see a sign they turn away and call it siḥrun mustamirr: magic that will soon pass, or magic that is powerful. Not just this sign: they were ready to reject every sign.

3.explain: They denied and followed their desires, not the evidence. Kullu amrin mustaqirr: every matter reaches a settled end, good with its people in Paradise, evil with its people in the Fire.

4.explain: The news of destroyed nations had already reached them in the Quran, with muzdajar in it: warnings strong enough to stop anyone from denial.

5.explain: Ḥikmatun bālighah: perfect wisdom, so no one is left with an excuse. Yet warnings do nothing for those who refuse to believe. It can also be read: what good do warnings do?

6.explain: So turn away from them (this came before fighting was permitted). Wait for the Day the Caller, Isrāfīl, calls them to something nukur: a horror unlike anything they have seen.

7.explain: Eyes lowered in terror, they come out of the ajdāth, the graves, like locusts spreading everywhere: countless, crowded together, not knowing where to go.

8.explain: Muhṭiʿīn: racing toward the Caller, necks stretched out, unable to hold back. The disbelievers say, “This is a hard Day”: hard for them, not for the believers.

9.explain: Before Makkah, Noah’s people denied Allah’s servant. They called him majnūn, mad, and wazdujir: he was rebuked and threatened, even with stoning if he did not stop.

10.explain: Maghlūb: overpowered. Few believed, and they could not resist the rest. So Noah called on his Lord: help me against them, and support Your religion.

11.explain: Allah opened the gates of the sky with munhamir water: pouring down in torrents, not falling from clouds the way rain normally does.

12.explain: The whole earth burst with springs, even ovens where fire had burned. The water of sky and earth met ʿalā amrin qad qudir: for a matter already decreed, the drowning of the deniers.

13.explain: Noah was carried on a ship of alwāḥ and dusur: planks, and the nails (or palm-fibre cords) that held them together.

14.explain: Tajrī bi-aʿyuninā: sailing under Our eyes, protected. A reward for the one who had been rejected, Noah. In another reading, the flood was the recompense of those who disbelieved.

15.explain: Taraknāhā: We left it as a sign, either the story of the flood or ships themselves, which people still ride. Fahal min muddakir: is there anyone who will take heed?

16.explain: A question that makes the listener admit it: how was My punishment, and My warning, which left no one an excuse?

17.explain: Yassarnā: We made the Quran easy, its words to memorize and recite, its meanings to understand and take heed from. No other revealed book is memorized whole by heart. So will anyone remember?

18.explain: ʿĀd, the people of Hūd, denied their messenger too. Before the punishment is even described, the question comes: how was My punishment and My warning?

19.explain: Innā arsalnā ʿalayhim: a ṣarṣar wind, freezing, roaring and violent, on a day of naḥs mustamirr: misfortune that went on for seven nights and eight days, until none were left.

20.explain: Tanziʿ an-nās: it plucked people up and threw them down on their heads. Their bodies lay like aʿjāz nakhl munqaʿir, palm trunks torn from the roots; ʿĀd were a tall people.

21.explain: The question again, now after the punishment: how was My punishment and warning? It was painful, and the warning left no excuse.

22.explain: The promise repeats, out of mercy: the Quran is made easy, so will anyone take heed? This ayah closes the first ruku.

23.explain: Thamūd, the people of Ṣāliḥ, denied bin-nudhur: the warnings he gave of what would happen if they refused to believe.

24.explain: Abasharan minnā wāḥidan: a human, just one of us, not an angel? Following him would mean ḍalāl wa suʿur: error and madness. They refused a human messenger, yet worshipped stones and trees.

25.explain: Why would adh-dhikr, the revelation, come to him alone out of all of us? No, he is kadhdhābun ashir: an arrogant, boastful liar who wants to rise above us.

26.explain: Ghadan, tomorrow, they will know who the arrogant liar really is: when the punishment falls, or on the Day of Judgement. In another reading it is Ṣāliḥ telling them: “You will know.”

27.explain: Innā mursilū an-nāqah: We are sending the she-camel out of the rock, as they had asked, as a fitnah, a test. So, Ṣāliḥ, watch what they do and be patient.

28.explain: Tell them the water is shared: one day for the camel, one day for them. Kullu shirbin muḥtaḍar: each side comes only on its own turn.

29.explain: They grew tired of it and called ṣāḥibahum, their companion, the most wretched of them. Fa-taʿāṭā: he took up his sword, fa-ʿaqar: and killed her, doing what they wanted.

30.explain: Fa-kayfa kāna ʿadhābī wa nudhur. In this story the question comes just before the punishment is described.

31.explain: One ṣayḥah, a single blast, and they became like hashīm al-muḥtaẓir: the dry twigs of a thorn fence built to pen livestock, trampled into crumbs and blown away.

32.explain: The third time: the Quran is made easy for remembrance. Is there anyone who will take heed?

33.explain: Lot’s people denied the warnings too. He called them to worship Allah alone and forbade an immoral act no people before them had done.

34.explain: Ḥāṣib: a wind hurling stones. Only Lot’s family was saved, bi-saḥar, in the last part of the night. Lot left with his daughters; his wife shared her people’s fate.

35.explain: Niʿmatan min ʿindinā: a favour from Allah. Kadhālika najzī man shakar: this is how He rewards whoever is grateful, believing in Him and obeying Him.

36.explain: Lot had warned them of baṭshatanā, Allah’s crushing grip, but fa-tamāraw bin-nudhur: they doubted, argued and rejected the warning.

37.explain: Angels came to Lot as handsome young guests, and his people demanded them. Allah wiped out their eyes, leaving their faces smooth where the eyes had been: “Taste My punishment and warning.”

38.explain: Ṣabbaḥahum bukratan: early in the morning a punishment struck, ʿadhābun mustaqirr: lasting, with no escape, carrying on into the Hereafter. Their towns were turned upside down.

39.explain: Fa-dhūqū ʿadhābī wa nudhur: taste My punishment and warning. It repeats 37, a command where the other stories ask a question.

40.explain: The fourth and last time: the Quran is made easy for remembrance; is there anyone who will take heed? This ayah closes the second ruku.

41.explain: Wa laqad jāʾa āla Firʿawna an-nudhur: warnings came to Pharaoh and his people, through Moses and Aaron, backed by great signs.

42.explain: They denied all Our signs, the nine given to Moses. So Allah seized them with the grip of one ʿAzīz, Mighty, and Muqtadir, All-Powerful, and drowned Pharaoh and his armies.

43.explain: Now Makkah is addressed: are your disbelievers better than those nations? Or is your barāʾah, immunity from punishment, written in the zubur, the revealed books? Neither is true.

44.explain: Or do they say, naḥnu jamīʿun muntaṣir: we are one united crowd, sure to win against anyone who opposes us?
44.why: Reportedly Abū Jahl spurred his horse ahead of the ranks at Badr, saying, “Today we win,” and 44–45 came down. Other reports place them in Makkah: a Companion only understood which crowd was meant when he saw the Prophet ﷺ recite them at Badr.

45.explain: Sa-yuhzamu al-jamʿ: the crowd will be routed and turn their backs. It happened as foretold: their army was defeated at Badr, and the Prophet ﷺ recited this ayah there in his armour.

46.explain: Bal as-sāʿatu mawʿiduhum: their real appointment is the Hour, and it is adhā wa amarr, more crushing and more bitter than any defeat in this world. This ayah was revealed in Makkah.

47.explain: Al-mujrimūn, the criminals, are in ḍalāl, lost from the truth, and suʿur: blazing fire (or madness). Thamūd used the same two words about following Ṣāliḥ (24).

48.explain: Yusḥabūn: dragged into the Fire on their faces, the noblest part of the body. They are told: dhūqū massa saqar, taste the touch of Saqar, a name of Hell.

49.explain: Innā kulla shayʾin khalaqnāhu bi-qadar: Allah created everything by measure and decree. He knew and wrote all that would happen, its time and its size, before creating it.
49.why: Reportedly the Quraysh idolaters came to argue with the Prophet ﷺ about qadar, divine decree, and ayat 47–49 came down in reply.

50.explain: Wa mā amrunā illā wāḥidah: Allah’s command is one word, “Be”, never repeated, and it happens ka-lamḥin bil-baṣar, faster than a blink. Bringing the Hour is no harder.

51.explain: Wa laqad ahlaknā ashyāʿakum: Allah destroyed your kind, nations who denied as you deny. His way with them is His way with you. Is there anyone who will take heed?

52.explain: Everything they did, good or bad, is in the zubur: the records kept by the angels.

53.explain: Every deed, ṣaghīr and kabīr, small and great, is mustaṭar: written down. Nothing is too small to be counted.

54.explain: Al-muttaqūn, the righteous, are in gardens and nahar: rivers of water, milk, honey and wine.

55.explain: Fī maqʿadi ṣidq: a seat of truth, free of idle and sinful talk, ʿinda malīkin muqtadir: near a King whose power is complete, able to give them whatever they wish.
